section_summary: The section concludes a statistical roster of educational institutions in Fukushima Prefecture, covering private schools for women and schools administered by ministries other than the Ministry of Education. It then supplies a map of northern Honshu, a two-sided archival charge-out record, and a handwritten comment criticizing a “high-flown” SCAP statement issued for the third anniversary of V-J Day. The roster reports founding dates, enrollment as of April and November 1946, and numbers of full- and part-time teachers.

subfiles.title: Roster of Japanese Educational Institutions, Fukushima Prefecture (continued)
subfiles.about: Tables list private and ministry-administered educational institutions in Fukushima Prefecture, with founding dates, enrollment, and teaching staffs.
subfiles.summary: Fukushima roster continued: private women's schools, male vocational institutes and youth schools under ministries, and the Kuntoen juvenile correction school, with April and November 1946 enrollment and teacher totals.

subfiles.title: Map of Northern Honshu
subfiles.about: A schematic map identifies prefectures, cities, prefectural capitals, large population centers, and institutions of higher learning in northern Honshu.
subfiles.summary: Map of Northern Honshu marking Niigata, Akita, Aomori, Yamagata, Fukushima, Sendai and other cities, prefectural capitals, places over 100,000 and higher education institutions.

subfiles.title: Description of Items Charged / Out
subfiles.about: A two-sided administrative form records the circulation or charging-out of archival files, including a reference to file 894.42(45-18).
subfiles.summary: Charge-out form DS-1033 with file numbers, dates and handwritten routing; names include Anderson, Mori, Kojima and Unterberger; dates into the 1970s.

subfiles.title: Handwritten note on a SCAP V-J Day anniversary statement
subfiles.about: The writer dismisses a SCAP statement for the third anniversary of V-J Day as high-flown and of little personal benefit.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten skeptical note on a SCAP V-J Day anniversary statement, initialed JMA; last line illegible.
